stretchable and breathable materials, enhancing
comfort and mobility. Other features include the use
of magnets and Velcro in place of buttons, making
it easier to put on and take off clothing. It also

Is it impossible to build an environment where
everyone
can
use
products
and
facilities
conveniently and without limitations? It was Ronald
Mace who sought the answer to this question. He
ⓐcontracted polio at the age of nine and spent the
rest of his life in a wheelchair. When studying
architecture at university, he struggled to access
some campus facilities due to inaccessible building
designs. This experience later ⓑinspired him to
invent the term universal design, which refers to
design for all. As an architect and product designer,
he pursued a world in which all products and
environments were designed to be artistic and
usable to the greatest extent possible by everyone,
regardless of their age, size, disability, nationality, or
language.
According to the principles of universal design, the
design must be able to be used equitably, flexibly,
simply, and ⓒintuitively by a wide variety of
people.
In
addition,
it
should
be
cognitively
accessible and minimize users’ physical efforts.
Finally, it requires the providing of sufficient space
for all users while reducing potential ⓓhazards and
adverse
consequences
from
accidental
or
unintended actions. A key ⓔfeature of universal
design is that this is not a special requirement only
for the benefit of a minority of the population. If
an environment is accessible, usable, convenient,
and a pleasure to use, everyone in the community
benefits.

다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?

How has universal design been incorporated into
modern architecture? One of the most representative
examples of universal design being used to improve
accessibility is the ramps installed in front of buildings.
Ramps, not stairs, are necessary for people with
disabilities who use wheelchairs, and they are also
beneficial for parents pushing strollers and the elderly.
Another example is automatic doors. They are
invaluable for those who rely on assistive devices
such as wheelchairs and crutches. They also provide
convenience for adults who have their hands full
and children who are not tall enough to open the
doors themselves. A further example is tactile paving.
These textured surfaces, often found on sidewalks,
steps,
and
crosswalks,
assist
visually
impaired
individuals by guiding them through urban spaces.

Did you know that one out of every ten people in
the world is left-handed? They face challenges in a
society designed for right-handed individuals. It is
inconvenient for them (A)[to use / using] some
right-handed products such as scissors, cameras,
and computer mice. The world we live in is
designed to be an environment suitable for what is
considered “(B)[normally / normal]” for the majority
of people, and it is filled with objects that are easy
for them to use. Thus, those who do not belong to
that category (C)[has / have] no choice but to live
with discomfort. In other words, a minority of
people with physical differences, such as the
left-handed, the disabled, and the elderly, either
endure inconvenience or deliberately seek objects
designed especially for them, which are often
difficult to find.
(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: to usenormallyhas
usingnormalhave
to usenormalhave
usingnormallyhas
to usenormalhas
solution: (A) 가주어 It에 대한 진목적어 자리에 쓰였으며, 앞에 의미상 주어 for them이 있으므로, ‘for+목적격’ 형태의 의미상 주어를 취하는 to부정사 to use가 적절하다. (B) ‘consider+목적어+(as/to be+)보어(~를 …하다고 여기다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘be considered+보어(…하다고 여겨지다)’를 이루 는 보어 자리이므로, 형용사 normal이 적절하다. 참고로, 보어 자리에 부사는 쓸 수 없다. Have you heard, “Hello, guys; let’s get started,” at
the beginning of a meeting? Could that make some
feel less included? Inclusive language is a respectful
way of communication by selecting words that
avoid bias, prejudice, and discrimination. Saying,
“Hello,
everyone,”
instead
of,
“Hello,
guys,”
demonstrates inclusivity, reduces potential barriers,
and enhances everyone’s sense of belonging.
Inclusive language promotes equality, respect, and
diversity, inviting all people to participate in society.
For example, replacing conventional terms with
racial implications like “blacklist” and “whitelist” with
neutral alternatives such as “deny list” and “allow
list”
enhances
inclusivity.
Similarly,
using
gender-neutral terms like “parent” and “guardian”
instead of “mom” and “dad” helps break down
biases and acknowledges diverse family structures.
Moreover, it is crucial to be aware of everyday
phrases that could be considered insensitive toward
individuals with medical conditions. For instance,
using “missed opportunity” instead of “blind spot”
or “ridiculous” rather than “crazy” demonstrates
more thoughtful communication.
As society becomes more inclusive, so must our
language. It is essential _______________________________
_______________________________. By being mindful of
the words we use, we can create a more welcoming
environment for everyone.

choices: to treat language as a fixed and unchangeablesystem
to prioritize semantic efficiency over socialsensitivity
to preserve traditional expressions regardless oftheir impact on society
tostayupdatedandtouseappropriatelanguage for our times
toensureclaritybyadheringstrictlytoconventional expressions

Have you heard, “Hello, guys; let’s get started,” at
the beginning of a meeting? Could that make some
feel less included? Inclusive language is a respectful

“Hello,
everyone,”
instead
of,
“Hello,
guys,”
demonstrates inclusivity, reduces potential barriers,
and enhances everyone’s sense of belonging.
Inclusive language promotes equality, respect, and
diversity, ⓑinvites all people to participate in
society. For example, replacing conventional terms
with racial implications like “blacklist” and “whitelist”
with neutral alternatives such as “deny list” and
“allow list” ⓒto enhance inclusivity. Similarly, using
gender-neutral terms like “parent” and “guardian”
instead of “mom” and “dad” helps break down
biases and acknowledges diverse family structures.
Moreover, it is crucial to be aware of everyday
phrases that ⓓcould consider insensitive toward
individuals with medical conditions. For instance,
using “missed opportunity” instead of “blind spot”
or “ridiculous” rather than “crazy” ⓔis demonstrated
more thoughtful communication.
As society becomes more inclusive, so must our
language. It is essential to stay updated and to use
appropriate language for our times. By being
mindful of the words we use, we can create a more
welcoming environment for everyone.

In baseball, the ball and the bat have hidden
numbers ⓐthat can greatly impact the outcome of
a game. A baseball has 108 double stitches,
creating ⓑraised lines on the ball called seams. The
seams help pitchers grip the ball better and transfer
more power and spin when throwing it. A spinning
ball can change directions in the air because of the
air pressure around it. This is called the Magnus
effect. The seams make this effect stronger. Pitchers
can use this effect ⓒto control the ball’s direction
and speed, creating pitches that are difficult for
batters to hit.
While pitchers try to throw challenging pitches by
utilizing the ball’s seams, batters attempt to make
contact with the ball accurately in the hope of
hitting a home run. The secret to hitting a home
run ⓓis lain in the baseball bat. The bat’s overall
length must be less than 106.8 cm long and the
diameter of the thickest part must be less than 7
cm. If a player ⓔwill hit the ball about 5-10 cm
from the end of the bat, the ball will fly the
farthest and give the player the most thrilling and
sweetest feeling. That is why this area is called the
“sweet spot.”

Is it impossible ⓐto build an environment where
everyone can use products and facilities conveniently
and without limitations? It was Ronald Mace ⓑwho
sought the answer to this question. He contracted
polio at the age of nine and spent the rest of his
life in a wheelchair. When ⓒstudying architecture at
university, he struggled to access some campus
facilities due to inaccessible building designs. This
experience later inspired him to invent the term
universal design, which ⓓrefer to design for all. As
an architect and product designer, he pursued a
world ⓔwhich all products and environments were
designed to be artistic and usable to the greatest
extent possible by everyone, regardless of their age,
size, disability, nationality, or language.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

body:
Have you heard, “Hello, guys; let’s get started,” at
the beginning of a meeting? Could that make
some feel less included? Inclusive language is a
respectful way of communication by selecting words
that avoid bias, prejudice, and discrimination.
Saying, “Hello, everyone,” instead of, “Hello, guys,”
demonstrates inclusivity, reduces potential barriers,
and enhances everyone’s sense of belonging.
(A) For instance, using “missed opportunity” instead
of “blind spot” or “ridiculous” rather than “crazy”
demonstrates more thoughtful communication.
As society becomes more inclusive, so must our
language. It is essential to stay updated and to
use appropriate language for our times. By being
mindful of the words we use, we can create a
more welcoming environment for everyone.
(B) Inclusive language promotes equality, respect,
and diversity, inviting all people to participate
in society. For example, replacing conventional
terms with racial implications like “blacklist”
and “whitelist” with neutral alternatives such as
“deny list” and “allow list” enhances inclusivity.
(C) Similarly, using gender-neutral terms like “parent”
and “guardian” instead of “mom” and “dad”
helps break down biases and acknowledges
diverse family structures. Moreover, it is crucial
to be aware of everyday phrases that could be
considered insensitive toward individuals with
medical conditions.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: “guys” 대신 “everyone”을 선택하는 것과 같은 포용적인 언어 의 사용은 포용성을 보여주고 잠재적인 장벽을 줄이며 모든 사람의 소속감을 높인다고 설명함으로써 포용적 언어의 필요 성과 효과에 대해 언급하는 주어진 글 다음에, 포용적 언어는 평등, 존중, 그리고 다양성을 장려하며 모든 사람이 참여하도 록 초대한다고 부연한 뒤 “blacklist”, “whitelist”와 같이 인종적 의미가 담긴 기존 용어를 “deny list”, “allow list”와 같은 중립 적인 용어로 대체함으로써 포용성을 높일 수 있다는 구체적 예시를 제시하는 (B), Similarly(마찬가지로) 다음에 “mom”, “dad” 대신 “parent”, “guardian”과 같은 성 중립적 용어를 사 용함으로써 편견을 깨고 다양한 가족 구조를 인정한다는 예시 를 추가 언급하고, 의학적 질환을 가진 개인에 대한 표현도 주 의해야 한다는 또 다른 관점을 제시하는 (C), For instance(예 를 들어) 다음에 (C)의 마지막에 언급된 내용과 관련해 “blind spot” 대신 “missed opportunity”를 사용하는 것 등의 예시를 제시하며 주장을 강화하고, 사회가 점점 더 포용적으로 변화함 에 따라 언어 역시 변화해야 한다는 점을 강조하면서 결론을 맺는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

Have you heard, “Hello, guys; let’s get started,” at
the beginning of a meeting? Could that make
some feel less included? Inclusive language is a
respectful way of communication by selecting words
that avoid bias, prejudice, and discrimination.
Saying, “Hello, everyone,” instead of, “Hello, guys,”
demonstrates inclusivity, reduces potential barriers,
and enhances everyone’s sense of belonging.
(A) For instance, using “missed opportunity” instead
of “blind spot” or “ridiculous” rather than “crazy”
demonstrates more thoughtful communication.
As society becomes more inclusive, so must our
language. It is essential to stay updated and to
use appropriate language for our times. By being
mindful of the words we use, we can create a
more welcoming environment for everyone.
(B) Inclusive language promotes equality, respect,
and diversity, inviting all people to participate
in society. For example, replacing conventional
terms with racial implications like “blacklist”
and “whitelist” with neutral alternatives such as
“deny list” and “allow list” enhances inclusivity.
(C) Similarly, using gender-neutral terms like “parent”
and “guardian” instead of “mom” and “dad”
helps break down biases and acknowledges
diverse family structures. Moreover, it is crucial
to be aware of everyday phrases that could be
considered insensitive toward individuals with
medical conditions.

(A)

unnoticed by the Korean sports industry. One
notable example of success is the Korean women’s
curling team. Following its debut at the Winter
Olympic Games of 2014, the team recognized the
need to enhance its sweeping technique. Sweeping
melts the ice and makes the stone move faster. If
too much ice melts, however, the stone moves too
fast and misses the target. On the other hand, if not
enough ice melts, the stone stops before reaching
the target. The amount of ice melting depends on
the sweeping speed and pressure. Applying too
much pressure slows down the sweeping speed,
and focusing only on speed makes it hard to
transfer enough force to the broom. Finding the
right balance between speed and pressure is
important to melt the right amount of ice.
(A)[Identify / To identify] the most effective
technique, the Korean team designed a sweeping
measurement
device.
The
device
consisted
of
infrared cameras and sensors attached to the
players’ bodies, shoes, and brooms. Through the
device and motion-capture screens, foot pressure
values and other data (B)[obtained / were obtained]
for analysis. After monitoring changes in the
temperature of the ice surface, the team concluded
(C)[that / what] speed was more economical than
strength for sweeping. The use of data analysis was
critical in the team’s winning of a silver medal at
the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics.

M: Welcome to our live show of the Nuri rocket
launch. I’m at the Naro Space Center with Dr.
Kim, the chief project manager. Hello, Dr. Kim.
Can you tell us about the Nuri rocket?
W: Yes, the Nuri rocket is a locally developed
rocket. We’re using our own space vehicles for
the first time.
M: We should all be proud. (A)Don’t you think so?
W: Sure. South Korea will be the world’s 7th nation
to place satellites into space using its own
technology.
M: Just now, an official announcement was made
that the launch was successful. This is incredible!
What will the Nuri rocket do in space?
W: It’ll place eight satellites into Earth’s orbit. It’ll
also
carry
out
missions,
such
as
ground
observation and space weather observation.
M: It’s a huge step forward for Korea’s space
science and technology. Thank you for talking
with us.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: Am I right?
Wouldn't you say so?
Are you following me?
Do you share this view?
Would you agree with me?
solution: 밑줄 친 ‘Don’t you think so?’는 ‘그렇게 생각하지 않니?’라는 뜻으로, 누리호가 국내에서 개발된 로켓이며, 처음으로 국내에 서 자체 개발한 우주선이 사용되고 있다는 것에 우리 모두가 자랑스러워해야 한다는 것에 동의하는지 묻는 표현이므로, 이 해 여부를 묻는 ❸ ‘Are you following me?(내말이 이해가 되 니?)’와는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 참고로, ‘Don’t you think so?’는 ‘Am I right?(내 말이 맞지?)’, ‘Wouldn’t you say so?(그렇게 말 하지 않겠니?(=그렇게 생각하지 않니?))’, ‘Do you share this view?(너도 같은 의견이니?)’, ‘Would you agree with me?(내 말에 동의하니?)’ 등으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.

Day 5 The World with No Gravity
Now I’m getting better at remembering where I am
when I first wake up. (A)________________, I’m still
often confused about how my body ⓐ[positions / is
positioned]. In the dark and without gravity, my
inner ear just takes a random guess as to my
position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that
I’m upside down. Of course, it’s actually my brain
readjusting to an environment where height and
weight lose their meaning. I can use any wall equally
as if each ⓑ[is / were] a floor. Everything has zero
weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to
lift huge objects with one finger as if I were a
superhero. (B)________________, zero gravity also makes
astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast.
That’s why I exercise for 150 minutes a day as my
colleagues ⓒ[do / are].

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)                      (B)
choices: ThusUnsurprisingly
MoreoverUnfortunately
HoweverFortunately
MoreoverFortunately
HoweverUnfortunately
solution: (A) 이제는 갓 깨어났을 때 내가 어디에 있는지 기억하는 능력 이 점점 좋아지고는 있다는 내용 다음에, 여전히 내 몸이 어떤 위치에 있는지 혼란스러울 때가 많다는 대조적인 내용이 이어 지므로, 빈칸에는 ‘하지만’이라는 뜻의 역접의 접속부사 However 가 알맞다. (B) 모든 것의 무게가 0이라서 날아다닐 수 있을 뿐 아니라 큰 사물들을 손가락 하나로 들어 올릴 수 있다는 무중력 상태의 장점 뒤에, 우주 비행사들의 근육과 골밀도를 매우 빠르게 감 소시키기도 한다는 무중력 상태의 단점이 이어지며 흐름이 반 전되므로, 빈칸에는 ‘불행하게도’라는 뜻의 접속부사 Unfortunately 가 알맞다.

solution: ⓐ 의문부사 how가 이끄는 간접의문문에서 주어 my body에 이어지는 동사 자리이며, 흐름상 현재시제가 쓰이는 것은 알맞 으나 주어인 my body(내 몸)가 타동사 position((특정 위치에) ~을 두다)의 대상이고 뒤에 목적어가 없으므로, 현재시제 수동 태인 is positioned가 알맞다. ⓑ 주절에 이어 구접속사 as if(마치 ~인 것처럼)가 이끄는 조 건절에서 주어 each에 대한 동사 자리로, 주절과 같은 시점에 서 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황을 가정해 ‘마치 각각의 벽이 바 닥인 것처럼’이라는 뜻을 나타내야 하므로, ‘as if+주어+과거동 사~’ 형태의 가정법 과거를 써야 한다. 또한, 가정법 과거 구 문에서 be동사는 인칭과 수에 관계없이 were를 써야 하므로, 가정법 과거동사 were가 알맞다. ⓒ 접속사 as(~하듯이)가 이끄는 부사절에서 주어 my colleagues에 이어지는 동사 자리로, 주절인 ‘I exercise ~ minutes’에서 ‘운동하다’의 의미로 쓰인 일반동사 exercise를 대신하는 대동사 do를 써야 하므로, 복수명사구인 주어 my colleagues에 수일치한 현재형의 복수동사 do가 알맞다.

Today’s mission required a spacewalk, one of the
riskiest ⓐtask on the ISS. We ⓑhad to install the
bases for some newly developed solar batteries on
the outside of the station.
Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a
room connected to the outside of the station, put
on our spacesuits, and ⓒfloated gently into space.
The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead,
looking like it was ready ⓓto come crashing down
upon us. Forcing myself to focus on the task, I
secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring just
outside the airlock. We moved along the handrail
to the edge of the station. The dark void in front
of us seemed ⓔendless. Despite the safety cable,
panic rose in me. I thought, “If my hand misses the
handrail, I will fall into the void.” The task seemed
to take forever, but I finally managed to install the
battery bases. When I turned my head, the bright
blue Earth was still there. In the middle of darkness,
its beauty was beyond description.

Today’s mission required a spacewalk, one of the
riskiest ⓐtask on the ISS. We ⓑhad to install the
bases for some newly developed solar batteries on
the outside of the station.
Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a
room connected to the outside of the station, put
on our spacesuits, and ⓒfloated gently into space.
The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead,
looking like it was ready ⓓto come crashing down
upon us. Forcing myself to focus on the task, I
secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring just
outside the airlock. We moved along the handrail
to the edge of the station. The dark void in front
of us seemed ⓔendless. Despite the safety cable,
panic rose in me. I thought, “If my hand misses the
handrail, I will fall into the void.” The task seemed
to take forever, but I finally managed to install the
battery bases. When I turned my head, the bright
blue Earth was still there. In the middle of darkness,
its beauty was beyond description.

it has been continuously occupied by astronauts. It

Hey there! Let me introduce you to a fascinating piece of
Korean history. Back on February 9, 1795, (A)[remarkable
something / something remarkable] happened in front of
Changdeokgung Palace, where King Jeongjo lived. There
was quite a crowd gathered there to witness a very special
procession that’s still talked about in Korea today.
Now, imagine this: more than 2,000 soldiers, hundreds
of horse riders, and lots of important officials, all
marching alongside the king and his mother with 50
musicians playing traditional instruments. When they
crossed a bridge (B)[made / making] of 36 boats on
the Hangang River, you can imagine how that turned
heads! That must (C)[be / have been] something
ordinary people rarely saw. Talk about a big event!
This was not just about putting on a show. No, it
was serious business. Lasting four days and covering
68 kilometers, the procession moved alongside the
king and his mother as they made a round trip to
Hwaseong Haenggung.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: remarkable somethingmadehave been
something remarkablemadebe
something remarkablemakinghave been
something remarkablemadehave been
remarkable somethingmakingbe
solution: (A) -thing으로 끝나는 부정대명사는 형용사의 후치 수식을 받 으므로, 형용사 remarkable이 부정대명사 something을 뒤에서 꾸 미는 something remarkable이 알맞다. (B) 문장의 동사로 crossed가 있으므로 흐름상 앞의 명사구 a bridge를 수식하는 분사(구)를 이루는 분사 자리이며, 수식을 받는 명사구가 ‘만들 어진’ 대상이므로, ‘make ~ of …(~을 …로 만들다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘~ be made of …(~가 …로 만들어지다)’를 이루는 과거분사 made가 알맞다. (C) 과거에 있었던 일에 대한 강한 추측을 나타내고 있으므로, 앞의 must와 함께 ‘~였음이 틀림없다’라는 뜻의 ‘must+have+ 과거분사’의 형태를 이루는 have been이 알맞다.

Stock market movement can be divided into two
major trends: bull market vs. bear market.
BULL MARKET
A bull market is a rising stock market situation
(A)[which / in which] economic conditions are
favorable to investors. They include high employment
rates, GDP increases, and other ⓐpositive economic
indicators. Think of a (B)[charged / charging] bull in
a field raising its horns. In a bull market, investors
often believe in the market’s present and future
performance. As such, they increase their stock
purchases and ⓑmaintain their investments.
BEAR MARKET
Like a standing bear having ⓒlowered its front
legs, a bear market implies a decline in stock
values. It occurs when economic conditions are not
favorable, and most stocks experience ⓓincreases in
value.
Factors
like
low
GDP
growth,
rising
unemployment, and
low
wages
are
ⓔpossible
conditions for a bear market. In difficult economic

of the stock market, which may lead them (C)[to

in whichchargingselling

(A)_______________, the more successful a business

of the company and start buying its stocks. As
demand for the stocks increases, so does the
stock price. In contrast, if a company performs

Understood.

there
any
other
factors

companies
are
constantly
under

system

the
entire

(A)
(B)

more about stocks. So how do we invest in

ⓐcalling a stock exchange, or stock market,
where you can easily buy or sell stocks in a
company. You might think investing in stocks
is an easy way to make a profit. But if you
are investing, you must be prepared ⓑto lose
money. Since the market constantly fluctuates,
there is a risk of loss and debt.
Neil: Investing in stocks is challenging! I bet our
listeners
are
curious
about
the
best
investment options though.

Generally, it would be smart to invest in
something that interests you, such as a
company behind some products you are into.
Always remember to do your research, stay
ⓒinformed about the companies you invest
in, and be mindful of your risk tolerance.
Neil: Investing can be a powerful tool for building
wealth, but it’s essential to approach it with
knowledge and caution.
Beth: Wise words, Neil.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Neil: I see. Then how do companies use the stock
market?
Beth: The stock market is (A)[important / unimportant]
for companies because it can provide them
with the money they need to grow and expand.
Neil: How does that work?
Beth: Let’s imagine that a small group of people
start a footwear company producing innovative
sneakers. The founders are (B)[doubtful /
confident] that their products will be popular
with consumers, but they do not have
enough funds to grow the business. So they
decide to put the newly formed company on
the stock market.
Neil: What happens then?
Beth: When a company is listed on the stock
market,
individuals
or
organizations
that
believe in the company’s bright future can
buy shares and become partial owners of the
company. This process makes it (C)[easy /
difficult] for the footwear company to raise
the funds it needs to grow its business. As
the business grows, the stock value rises, and
the stockholders’ profits increase.
(A)
(B)           (C)

importantconfidentdifficult
unimportantdoubtfuldifficult
importantdoubtfuleasy
importantconfidenteasy
solution: (A) 주식 시장이 회사가 성장하고 확장하는 데 필요한 자금을 제공할 수 있다고 했으므로, 이에 근거하여 주식 시장이 회사 에 중요하다는 흐름이 되는 important(중요한)가 알맞다. (B) 역접의 접속사 but(그러나)으로 연결해 창업자들이 사업을 성장시킬 충분한 자금을 갖고 있지 않다는 내용이 이어지므로, 창업자들이 그들의 제품이 소비자에게 인기 있을 것이라 자신 한다는 대조적인 흐름이 되는 confident(확신하는)가 알맞다. (C) 신발 회사가 주식 시장에 상장되어 회사의 밝은 미래를 믿 는 개인이나 기관이 주식을 사는 것의 결과가 이어져야 하므 로, 그 회사가 사업을 성장시킬 자금을 쉽게 모을 수 있다는 흐름이 되는 easy(쉬운)가 알맞다.

that이 쓰였음 14) ⑤: 주식이 한 회사 소유권의 일부 지분을 나타내며, 주주 들이 회사 경영에 적극적으로 참여할 수는 없지만, 회 사가 중요한 결정을 할 때 의견을 낼 수 있음이 언급 되므로, 글의 주제로 ⑤ ‘주식의 정의와 주주들의 역할’ 이 알맞다. 오답 ① 주주 총회를 조직하는 과정 ② 전문 경영인들을 선호하는 이유들 ③ 다양한 회사의 주식들을 매수하기 위한 전략들 ④ 회사의 지분들을 소유하는 것의 위험들과 이점들 본문변형 지문의 첫 문장 ‘Okay, let’s start with the concept of a stock.’을 삭제함 15) (1) ⓐ calling → called (2) ⓓ making → make : ⓐ 앞에 문장의 동사(can buy)가 있으므로 앞의 명사(구) 를 수식하는 분사(구)를 이루는 자리이며, 수식을 받는 명 사구인 an official place(공식 장소)가 ‘불리는’ 대상이고 뒤에 온 a stock exchange, or stock market은 목적어가 아니라 ‘call A B(A를 B라고 부르다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘A be called B(A가 B라고 불리다)’에서 보어(B)에 해당하는 명사구이므로, 과거분사 called로 고친다. ⓓ 뒤에 술어동사가 따로 존재하지 않으므로, 동사원형으 로 시작하는 명령문을 이루는 make로 고친다. 16) ②: 주식 투자에 있어서 시장이 끊임없이 변동하기 때문에 손실과 부채의 위험이 있다고 했으므로, ② ‘주식 시장 은 일반적으로 예측 가능하고, 주식 가치가 자주 변하 지 않는다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 주식은 주식 거래소와 같은 공식 장소를 통해 거래 될 수 있다. ③ 개인 상황들이 무엇이 최고의 투자 선택들인지를 결정한다. ④ Beth는 당신이 관심 있는 회사들에 투자하는 것이 현명할 수 있다고 시사한다. ⑤ Neil은 투자할 때 지식과 신중함 둘 다의 중요성을 강조한다. 17) ③: 주식 시장의 움직임은 강세장과 약세장의 두 가지 주요 추세로 구분될 수 있으며, 강세장은 경제적인 조건이 투자자에게 유리한 상승하는 주식 시장 상황이라는 주 어진 글에 이어, 경제적인 조건들을 They로 받아 그 사 례들을 나열하는 내용과, 머리 뿔을 들어 올리고 들판 에서 돌진하는 황소처럼, 상승장에서 투자자들이 시장 의 현재와 미래 성과에 대해 믿는다는 (B), (B)의 마지 막 문장에 근거하여 투자자들에 해당하는 they(그들)가 주식 매입을 늘리고 투자를 유지한다는 내용과, 역접의 연결어 On the other hand(반면에)에 이어 앞다리를 내린 채 서 있는 곰처럼, 하락장이 주식 가치의 하락을 암시하며 경제적 조건들이 좋지 않을 때 발생하고 주식 대부분이 가치 하락을 겪는다는 (C), 경제적 조건들을 Factors로 받아 그 사례들을 나열하는 내용과, 어려운 경제 상황에서 투자자들이 주식 시장을 부정적으로 보 며 주식을 매도하게 된다는 (A)의 흐름이 자연스럽다. 18) ⑤: (A) 주식 시장이 회사가 성장하고 확장하는 데 필요한 자금을 제공할 수 있다고 했으므로, 이에 근거하여 주 식 시장이 회사에 중요하다는 흐름이 되는 important (중요한)가 알맞다. unimportant 중요하지 않은 본문변형 very important → important (B) 역접의 접속사 but(그러나)으로 연결해 창업자들이 사업을 성장시킬 충분한 자금을 갖고 있지 않다는 내 용이 이어지므로, 창업자들이 그들의 제품이 소비자에 게 인기 있을 것이라 자신한다는 대조적인 흐름이 되 는 confident(확신하는)가 알맞다. doubtful 확신이 없는 (C) 신발 회사가 주식 시장에 상장되어 회사의 밝은 미 래를 믿는 개인이나 기관이 주식을 사는 것의 결과가 이어져야 하므로, 그 회사가 사업을 성장시킬 자금을 쉽게 모을 수 있다는 흐름이 되는 easy(쉬운)가 알맞다. difficult 어려운 19) ②: 주식 시장이 계속 변동하기 때문에 손실과 부채의 위험 이 있음을 인식해야 하며, 관심 있는 회사의 주식을 사 되 그 회사에 대한 지식을 바탕으로 신중하게 투자해야 함이 강조되므로, 글의 주제로 ② ‘현명한 주식 투자자 가 되기 위한 전략들’이 알맞다. 오답 ① 재정적 손실의 심리적 영향 ③ 회사의 총자산을 평가하는 방법들 ④ 투자를 위한 유망 기업들을 식별하는 방법들 ⑤ 공식 주식 거래소들과 사설 시장들의 비교 20) ②: 한 회사의 주주가 되면 그 회사의 소유권 일부분을 갖 게 되는 것이라고 했으므로, 회사 주식을 회사의 파이 에 빗대어 설명하는 ② ‘그 회사의 파이 한 조각을 가 지는 것’이 알맞다. 오답 ① 지역 은행으로부터 돈을 빌리는 것 ③ 소비자들에게 완제품을 판매하는 것 ④ 기업의 전문 경영인이 되는 것 ⑤ 회사 전체의 예산을 통제하는 것

walking tour organized by the community center?
B: No, what is it?
G: It’s an amazing walking tour ⓑwhich you can learn
about the history and culture of our city.
B: Sounds interesting! When is it?
G: It’s on Saturday, June 22, and it starts at the
community center.
B: I’m available on that day. ⓒTell me more.
G: An outer city course and a central city course ⓓare
being offered. Which one are you interested in?
B: I’d like to explore the outer city. I ⓔhaven’t had
the chance to do that much.
G: Great choice! The community center offers both
one-hour and two-hour courses for the outer city
course.
B: I’m up for the two-hour course.
G: Perfect! You can sign up online on the community
center’s website.
B: I’ll do that right away. I’m glad ⓕto knowing about
this wonderful opportunity.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ which → where 또는 on which (완전한 절(you ~ city)을 이끌어, 선행사인 명사구 an amazing walking tour를 수식하는 관계사절 을 이루어야 하므로, 관계대명사 which를 장소나 상황을 나타내는 선행사와 쓰이는 관계부사 where로 고치거나, 선행사에 어울리는 전치사를 사용해 ‘전치사+관계대명사’인 on which로 고친다.) ⓕ to knowing → to know(감정 형용사인 glad 뒤에 ‘알게 되 어’라는 의미로 감정의 원인이나 이유를 나타내는 부사적 용법 의 to부정사(to+동사원형)가 와야 하므로, to knowing을 to know로 고친다.)

wasn’t just some fancy show for ordinary people. It
was actually a way for them to get up close and
personal with the king.
(A) And here’s the cherry on top: through the
procession, King Jeongjo made government more
accessible. During that time, the government
used to hold exams to hire officials every three
years.
(B)
So, there weren’t many chances available. He
added special exams during the procession,
giving more people a shot at joining the
government. This move was innovative back
then and made the government more diverse.
(C) King Jeongjo set up a chance during the
procession for common people to meet him
and to share their concerns. This was a big
deal, especially for those who couldn’t read or
write. They didn’t have any other way to tell
the king what was on their minds, so this was
a direct line to him.

In baseball, the ball and the bat have hidden
numbers ⓐthat can greatly impact the outcome of
a game. A baseball has 108 double stitches,
creating raised lines on the ball ⓑare called seams.
The seams help pitchers grip the ball better and
transfer more power and spin when throwing it. A
spinning ball can change directions in the air
because of the air pressure around it. This is called
the Magnus effect. The seams make this effect
stronger. Pitchers can use this effect to control the
ball’s direction and speed, ⓒmade pitches that are
difficult for batters to hit.
While pitchers try to throw challenging pitches by
utilizing the ball’s seams, batters attempt to make
contact with the ball accurately in the hope of
hitting a home run. The secret to ⓓhit a home run
lies in the baseball bat. The bat’s overall length
must be less than 106.8 cm long and the diameter
of the thickest part must be less than 7 cm. If a
player hits the ball about 5-10 cm from the end of
the bat, the ball will fly the farthest and ⓔgive the
player the most thrilling and sweetest feeling. That
is ⓕwhy this area is called the “sweet spot.”

transfer more power and spin when throwing it. A
spinning ball can change directions in the air
because of the air pressure around it. This is called
the Magnus effect. The seams make this effect
stronger. Pitchers can use this effect to control the
ball’s direction and speed, ⓒmade pitches that are
difficult for batters to hit.
While pitchers try to throw challenging pitches by
utilizing the ball’s seams, batters attempt to make
contact with the ball accurately in the hope of
hitting a home run. The secret to ⓓhit a home run
lies in the baseball bat. The bat’s overall length
must be less than 106.8 cm long and the diameter
of the thickest part must be less than 7 cm. If a
player hits the ball about 5-10 cm from the end of
the bat, the ball will fly the farthest and ⓔgive the
player the most thrilling and sweetest feeling. That
is ⓕwhy this area is called the “sweet spot.”

decades. However, the team turned to sports
analytics to maintain its edge over its rivals in
preparation for the 2020 Tokyo Olympics. The team
developed a system to monitor players’ heart rates
by using advanced visual computing technology to
convert facial color variations into heart rates. This
data was used for psychological training to help
players maintain stable heart rates during crucial
moments.
The team also created an AI coach that helped
adjust shooting form. The team managers requested
that the AI coach edit training videos of the players
to assist with practical analysis. Players and coaches
used the edited videos to analyze the players’ usual
habits or weaknesses. The (B)_______________ use of
data analysis by the Korean women’s archery team
handed them their ninth Olympic gold medal in a
row in Tokyo.

(B)

podcast for teenagers! I’m your host, Neil.
Thank you for tuning in. We have a very special
guest with us, the renowned economist Beth
Friedman. Please give her a warm welcome!
Beth: Hello, everyone. It’s truly an honor to be here
with all of you.
Neil: We’ve been exploring the basics of economics.
In this 35th episode, we’ll be talking about the
world of stocks. So let’s get started.
Beth: Before we begin, Neil, I have a question for
you. Have you ever wondered what to do
with your extra money?
Neil: Absolutely, Beth. I bet all our listeners have
asked themselves the same question.
Beth: Indeed. It’s a question that often arises, especially
among young people who are beginning to
explore the world of finance. As you go about
your daily lives, (A)여러분은 자신이 물건을 구매
하는 것과 버스 요금을 지불하는 것과 같은 금
융 활동들에 참여된 것을 발견하게 됩니다. After
that, you might have some extra money.
Neil: You’re right. Some people might save it in the
bank, and others might prefer keeping it in
their wallets for immediate use. There are also
a few who have already been venturing into
stock trading. Today, we’re going to provide you
with an overview of stocks and stock markets,
enabling you to gain insight into the economy.

body:
Mother Earth didn’t exactly welcome us back with
open arms. Earth’s atmosphere is resistant to objects
entering from space. Any object will create enough
friction simply ⓐto burn up from the heat. This
protects the planet from the orbital debris that
would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant
we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere
ⓑthat created temperatures up to 1650 degrees
Celsius.
After pushing our spaceship away from the station,
we eased our way into the upper layers of the
atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity
ⓒto begin returning. My watch felt a lot heavier on
my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule
heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces
flew by the window, which was scorched black. We
were falling faster than the speed of sound. Once we
got inside the atmosphere about eight kilometers
above the planet, a parachute caught us with a
sudden halt and dragged and swung our capsule
wildly through the sky until we hit the ground.
It’s hard to describe how heavy everything felt in
those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt
terribly heavy, and so did my legs. ⓓGet used to
gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a
long time. The important thing is I’m home. I can
smell the grass and ⓔfeel the wind and the rain!
I’ll remember how magical these things are for the
rest of my life.

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

Now I’m getting better at remembering where I
am when I first wake up, but I’m still often
confused about how my body is positioned. In the
dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a
random guess as to my position, and sometimes I
wake up convinced that I’m upside down.
(A) This enables me not only to fly but also to lift
huge objects with one finger as if I were a
superhero.
(B) Of course, it’s actually my brain readjusting to
an environment where height and weight lose
their meaning. I can use any wall equally as if
each were a floor. Everything has zero weight.
(C) Unfortunately, zero gravity also makes astronauts
lose muscle and bone density really fast. That’s
why I exercise for 150 minutes a day as my
colleagues do.
solution: 이제는 갓 깨어났을 때 글쓴이 자신이 어디에 있는지 기억하 는 능력이 점점 좋아지고는 있지만 여전히 몸이 어떤 위치에 있는지 혼란스러울 때가 많으며, 어둠과 무중력 속에서 내부 귀는 그저 되는대로 글쓴이의 위치를 추측해서 때때로 자신이 거꾸로 놓인 걸로 확신하며 잠에서 깨곤 한다는 내용의 주어 진 글에 이어, 앞에 언급된 글쓴이의 신체 작용과 관련된 내용 을 it으로 받아 물론 그것이 실제로는 높이나 무게가 의미를 잃는 환경에 글쓴이의 뇌가 재적응하는 과정이라고 설명한 뒤, 글쓴이가 어떤 벽이건 똑같이 바닥인 것처럼 사용할 수 있으 며, 모든 것이 무게가 0이라는 내용을 언급하는 (B), 앞의 모든 것의 무게가 0이라는 내용을 This로 받아, 그것이 글쓴이로 하 여금 날아다닐 수 있도록, 그리고 큰 사물들을 손가락 하나로 들어올릴 수 있도록 한다는 (A), 접속부사 Unfortunately(불행 하게도)에 연결된 대조적인 내용이자 (A)에 대한 추가 언급으 로서 부사 also(또한)를 사용하여, 무중력 상태가 우주 비행사 들의 근육과 골밀도를 매우 빠르게 감소시킨다는 내용과, 그것 이 글쓴이가 동료들처럼 매일 150분씩 운동을 하는 이유라고 설명하는 (C)의 흐름이 자연스럽다. body:
The International Space Station, or ISS, is the ninth
space station to be inhabited by humans. Since
2000, it has been continuously occupied by astronauts.
It serves as a research laboratory for many fields,
including astronomy, physics, and medicine. It is
also used ⓐto test spacecraft systems required for
possible future missions to the moon, Mars, and
asteroids. As (A)[big / small] as a football field, it
ⓑcomposes of many different sections, such as
experiment
modules,
habitation
modules,
solar
battery panels, and robotic arms. It is a completely
unique structure assembled by spacewalkers ⓒflied
around Earth at 28,000 kilometers per hour in a
vacuum in extremes of temperature of plus and
minus 270 degrees Celsius. It is the result of work
by 15 different nations over about two decades.
The work was carried out by thousands of people
speaking different languages and ⓓusing different
engineering methods and standards. Putting the
space station into orbit, making it ⓔto work, and
keeping it working are perhaps some of the
(B)[easiest / most difficult] things that human beings
have ever done. In January 2022, NASA announced
a plan to de-orbit the ISS in 2030. Many astronauts
believe ⓕthat it will stand forever as proof that
when humans work (C)[together / independently],
we can do anything from going to Mars to solving
our problems here on Earth.

major trends: bull market vs. bear market.
BULL MARKET
A bull market is a rising stock market situation in
which
economic
conditions
are
favorable
to
investors. They include high employment rates, GDP

Think of a charging bull in a field raising its horns.

they increase their stock purchases and maintain
their investments.
BEAR MARKET

a bear market implies a decline in stock values. It

and most stocks experience decreases in value.

market. In difficult economic situations, investors
frequently have negative views of the stock market,

영어I YBM(박준언) 2과 예상문제 3회 - 객관식(선다형) 1. ② 2. ①, ③ 3. ④ 4. ③, ⑤ 5. ③, ⑤ 6. ⑤ 7. 주관식 8. ⑤ 9. ⑤ 10. ② 11. ② 12. ③ 13. 주관식 14. ⑤ 15. ③ 16. ③ 17. ④ 18. ④ 19. 주관식 20. ⑤ 정답 및 해설 ┃3회┃ 1) ②: 어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다. ⓔ was → were (주어부 ‘the sneakers I got’에 이어진 문장의 동사 자리로, 주어부의 핵심 단어인 sneakers가 복수명사이므로, 이에 수일치된 복수동사 were로 고친다.) ⓕ affording → afford 또는 to afford (과거형 동사 helped와 목적어 me에 이어져 ‘help+목적어+목적격보 어’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, help는 목적격보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사를 취하는 동사이므 로 afford나 to afford로 고친다.) *원래 지문에는 afford가 쓰였음 2) ①, ③ : 십 대들은 갖고 싶은 것이 많지만 예산이 한정되어 있어서 돈을 모으는 것이 어려울 수 있다고 했으므로, ① ‘십 대들 은 충분한 예산을 보유하고 있음에도 불구하고 돈을 모으 는 데 어려움을 겪는다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 또한, 저축 계좌를 만들라고 조언하며 은행이 언제든지 돈 을 인출할 수 있게 해준다고 했으므로, ③ ‘일단 자금이 저 축 계좌에 입금되면, 장기간 동안 인출될 수 없다.’도 일치 하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ② 은행은 사람들의 예금을 안전하게 보관하고 그들의 예 금들에 대한 이자를 제공한다. ④ 돈 관리 앱을 활용하는 것은 사람들이 자신들의 자금이 정확히 어디에 지출되는지 추적할 수 있게 해 준다. ⑤ 간식들을 사기보다 집에서 식사하는 것이 효과적인 저 축 전략으로 권장된다. 3) ④: ⓒ explored → exploring (주어인 We가 ‘~을 탐구하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어인 the basics of economics가 이 어지고 있으므로, 앞의 have been과 현재완료 진행형을 이루는 현재분사 exploring으로 고친다.) ⓕ what → that (bet의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절을 이끌고 있으므로, 명사절 접속사인 that으로 고친다. 참 고로, 관계대명사 또는 의문대명사 what은 뒤에 주어나 목적어, 보어가 없는 불완전한 절이 이어져야 한다.) 본문변형 ⓕ는 명사절 접속사로 원래 지문에서 생략되어 있음 4) ③, ⑤ : Neil이 이번 에피소드를 35회라고 언급했으므로, ③ ‘이것 은 ‘10분 경제학 101’ 시리즈의 첫 번째 에피소드이다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 또한, 대화를 시작하기 전에 Beth가 Neil에게 여분의 돈으 로 무엇을 할 것인지 궁금해 본 적 있는지 질문하므로, ⑤ ‘대화를 시작하기 위해, Neil은 Beth에게 여분의 돈을 관리 하는 것에 관한 질문을 한다.’도 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 그 팟캐스트의 주요 청취자는 십 대들이다. ② Beth Friedman은 그 팟캐스트에 손님으로 초대된 유명 한 경제학자이다. ④ 그들은 주요 주제로서 주식의 세계에 중점을 둘 것이다. 5) ③, ⑤ : 회사들은 원자재 가격, 생산 기술의 발전 및 인건비와 같 은 시장 요인들의 영향을 지속해서 받고 있다고 했으므로, ③ ‘생산 기술의 발전은 주가를 안정시키는 유일한 요인이 다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 또한, 원자재 가격이 오르면 생산 비용과 소비자 시장에서 의 가격 상승으로 인해 실적 부진으로 이어질 수 있다고 했으므로, ⑤ ‘회사들은 원자재들의 가격이 오를 때 재정적 으로 이득을 얻는다.’도 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 주식의 가치는 수요와 공급 사이의 균형에 의해 결정된 다. ② 회사의 좋은 재정적 성과는 더 많은 투자자들을 끌어들 이는 경향이 있다. ④ 상승하는 고무 가격은 신발 회사의 생산 비용을 증가시 킬 수 있다. 6) ⑤: ⓔ dismiss(~을 일축하다) → seek(~을 구하다) 7) Does that mean stockholders themselves can actively participate in the management : ··명사절 접속사는 생략하라는 <조건>에 따라, 타동사 mean의 목적어로 명사절 접속사 that이 생략된 완전한 절이 이어지도록 영작한다. ··강조 용법의 재귀대명사를 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라, ‘주주 자신들’을 나타내기 위해 주어인 stockholders의 뒤 에 이를 강조하는 재귀대명사 themselves를 쓴다. ··‘~에 참여하다’라는 뜻의 ‘participate in ~’을 활용한다. 8) ⑤: (A) 앞에 절의 술어동사(start)가 존재하므로, 앞의 명사구 a footwear company를 수식하는 분사구를 이끄는 현재 분사 producing이 알맞다. (B) 형용사 confident 뒤에서 완전한 절(their products will be popular with consumers)을 이끌고 있으므로 접 속사 that이 알맞다. 관계대명사 또는 의문대명사 what 은 뒤에 주어나 목적어, 보어가 없는 불완전한 절이 이 어져야 한다. 영어I YBM(박준언) 2과 예상문제 3회 - 주관식(서답형) 7. Does that mean stockholders themselves can actively participate in the management 13. There are, a few who[that] have already been venturing into stock trading 18. (1) the market constantly fluctuates, there is a risk of loss and debt (2) behind some products they are into (C) 주어 a company(한 회사)가 ‘(목록에) 올려지는’ 대상 이며 뒤에 목적어 없이 전치사구 on the stock market이 이어지므로, 수동태인 is listed가 알맞다. 9) ⑤: 주식 시장이 회사가 성장하고 확장하는 데 필요한 자금 을 제공할 수 있다고 했으며, 사업을 성장시킬 자금이 부족한 신생 회사가 상장되는 결정을 내리는 것이 가정 되므로, 회사가 주식 시장에 상장되어 그 회사의 가능성 을 믿는 개인이나 기관이 주식을 사는 과정은 회사가 성 장에 필요한 자금을 모으는 데 도움을 준다는 흐름이 되 는 ⑤ ‘그 신발 회사가 자신의 사업을 성장시키는 데 필 요한 자금을 모으는 것을 쉽게 만들어 준다’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 생산 시설들을 해외로 확장하는 회사의 능력을 제한 한다 ② 회사가 수요와 공급의 법칙에 의해 영향을 받는 것을 방지한다 ③ 모든 투자자가 매달 고정된 금액의 수익을 받을 것을 보장한다 ④ 창업자들이 이익을 나누지 않고 회사의 완전한 소유 권을 유지하게 해준다 10) ②: 주어진 문장은 ‘반대로, 만약 회사가 실망스럽게 성과를 내면, 주가도 하락할 것입니다.’라는 뜻이며, ‘반대로’를 뜻하는 역접의 접속부사구 In contrast로 시작하므로, 회사의 사업이 성공하여 주식에 대한 수요가 증가하면 주가도 오르게 된다는 대조적인 내용 뒤이자, 회사의 성과 외에 주식 가격에 영향을 미치는 다른 요인들에 대해 묻는 내용 앞인 (B)에 들어가야 한다. 11) ②: 주식에 대해 배울수록 더 어려워지는 것 같다고 말하며 주식 시장에 투자하는 법을 묻는 내용의 주어진 글 다 음에, 주어진 글의 마지막 말에 대해 주식 거래소나 주 식 시장이라는 공식 장소에서 주식을 쉽게 사고팔 수 있다는 내용과, 주식 투자가 수익을 얻는 쉬운 방법이 라고 생각할 수 있지만 시장의 변동성 때문에 손실과 부채의 위험을 각오해야 한다는 Beth의 말에 이어, Neil 이 최고의 투자 선택에 대해 묻는 (B), (B)의 최고의 투 자 선택을 That으로 받아 그것이 개인 상황에 달려있다 는 내용과, 관심을 끄는 회사에 투자하는 것이 현명하 며 조사 및 투자하는 회사에 대한 정보, 투자 위험 허 용 범위에 대한 인식이 필요하다는 Beth의 말에 이어, Neil이 투자가 부를 쌓는 강력한 도구지만 지식과 신중 한 접근이 필수적이라고 말하는 (A), (A)의 마지막 말에 대해 Beth가 현명한 말씀이라고 답하는 내용과, Neil이 오늘 방송의 마무리와 다음 방송의 예고를 하며, 이 방 송이 도움이 되었다면 경제학 공부에 관심 있을 친구들 과 공유해 달라고 말하는 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연 스럽다. 12) ③: ⓐ Beth가 긍정의 대답과 함께 그 질문이 종종 특히 금 융의 세계를 탐색하기 시작하는 젊은이들 사이에서 제 기된다고 말하는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, Neil이 모든 청취자가 같은 질문을 스스로에게 해 본 적 있다고 생 각한다는 흐름이 적절하다. 따라서 빈칸에는 assume(~ 을 추정한다), bet(~을 장담한다), guarantee(~을 보장 한다)가 알맞다. ⓑ 이후에 일어나는 일로서 여분의 돈이 좀 생길 수 있 다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 일상생활을 하면서, 물건 구매나 버스 요금 지불과 같은 금융 활동에 참여하는 자신을 발견하게 된다는 흐름이 적절하다. 따라서 빈칸 에는 ‘engaged in ~(~에 참여하는)’, ‘involved in ~(~에 연루된)’이 알맞다. 오답 ① ~을 부인한다 ~로부터 거리를 두는 ② ~을 추정한다 ~에 무관심한 ④ ~을 의심한다 ~에 연루된 ⑤ ~을 보장한다 ~로부터 떨어져 있는 13) There are, a few who[that] have already been venturing into stock trading : ··‘~(들)이 있다’라는 뜻의 유도부사 구문인 ‘there is/are+ 주어 ~’를 활용하되, ‘몇몇 (사람들)’을 나타내기 위해 복 수의 부정대명사구 a few를 주어 자리에 쓴다. ··주격 관계대명사를 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라, a few 를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사 who나 that이 이끄는 관계사절을 영작한다. *원래 지문에는 who가 쓰였음 ··‘~에 뛰어들다’라는 뜻의 구동사 ‘venture into ~’를 활 용하되, 현재완료 진행형을 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라, ‘have been+현재분사’의 형태가 되도록 영작한다. 14) ⑤: 팟캐스트의 진행자인 Neil이 이번 에피소드의 특별 손 님인 경제학자 Beth Friedman을 소개한 후 대화를 나 누며 오늘 주식과 주식 시장에 대해 알아볼 예정이라 고 설명하므로, 글의 주제로 ⑤ ‘초대 손님인 경제학자 Beth Friedman과 함께하는 십 대 친화적인 주식 입문’ 이 알맞다. 오답 ① 십 대들이 여분의 돈을 저축하는 다양한 방법들 ② 주식 시장에 대한 조기 투자의 중요성 ③ 주식 시장의 변동성이 젊은 투자자들에게 미치는 영향 ④ Beth Friedman처럼 유명한 경제학자가 되기 위한 조언들 15) ③: 어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다. ⓑ do → does (‘~도 또한 그렇다’라는 뜻의 도치 구문 으로 일반동사가 사용된 경우 ‘so+do/does/did+주어’의 형태가 되어야 하므로, 주어인 단수명사구 the stock price에 수일치된 단수동사 does로 고친다.) ⓓ lead → leads (주어 This와 부사구 in turn에 이어지 는 단수동사 affects와 등위접속사 and로 병렬연결되며, 뒤에 ‘자동사+전치사’ 구조의 ‘lead to ~’(~로 이어지다) 를 이루는 전치사 to의 전치사구가 이어지므로 능동태 의 단수동사인 leads로 고친다.) 16) ③: (A) 주식 가격이 공급과 수요의 법칙에 따라 결정된다 고 했으므로, 사업이 성공할수록 더 많은 사람이 그 회 사의 주식을 사기 시작할 것이라는 흐름이 되는 more (더 많은)가 알맞다. less 더 적은 (B) 회사가 실적 부진에 시달리게 되어 주식 가격이 하 락한다는 결과가 뒤에 이어지므로, 소비자들이 그 회사 의 운동화를 구매하는 것을 망설인다는 흐름이 되는 hesitate(주저한다)가 알맞다. rush 서두르다 (C) 점점 많은 사람들이 비즈니스 투명성, 환경 친화성, 사회 정의와 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

In King Jeongjo’s mind (B)[was / were] big plans

the political chaos in Hanyang. So King Jeongjo

(A)          (B)
(C)
choices: thatwerebring
whichwereto bring
whichwerebring
thatwasto bring
whichwasbring
solution: (A) 쉼표 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was being built)을 이끌어 앞 절의 Hwaseong Fortress에 대한 부연 설명을 하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로, 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. 참고로 that은 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 사용하지 않으며, 완전한 절(the ~ Fortress)에 접속사 없이 쉼 표로만 다른 완전한 절이 이어질 수 없으므로 동사 was에 대 한 주어인 지시대명사 that도 될 수 없다. (B) 강조를 위해 장소의 부사구 In King Jeongjo’s mind가 문두 에 오면서 ‘부사구+be동사+주어’의 도치 어순을 이루는 be동사 자리로, 주어부 big plans for Hwaseong에서 핵심어인 plans가 복수명사이므로, 이에 수일치된 복수동사 were가 알맞다. (C) 동사 let과 목적어 them에 이어져 ‘let+목적어+목적격보어(~ 가 …하게 하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 목 적어 them이 ‘타동사+부사’ 구조의 구동사 ‘bring ~ together(~ 을 합치다)’의 주체이고 부사 together 뒤에 목적어인 명사구 ‘the finest ~ West’가 이어지므로, 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 bring이 알맞다. 참고로, 사역동사 let의 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동 관계이면 목적격보어 자리에 be p.p.가 쓰인다.

body:
Let’s go back to the procession. The procession
wasn’t just some fancy show for ordinary people. It
was actually a way for them to get up close and
personal with the king. King Jeongjo set up a
chance during the procession for common people
to meet him and to share their concerns. This was
a big deal, especially for those who couldn’t read
or write. They didn’t have any other way to tell the
king what was on their minds, so this was a direct
line to him.
And here’s ⓐ______________________________: through
the procession, King Jeongjo made government
more accessible. During that time, the government
used to hold exams to hire officials every three
years. So, there weren’t many chances available. He
added special exams during the procession, giving
more people a shot at joining the government. This
move was innovative back then and made the
government more diverse.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the last straw
the cherry on top
a blessing in disguise
a double-edged sword
the calm before the storm
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Suwon Hwaseong stands proudly as a UNESCO
World Heritage Site, but its uniqueness often goes
unnoticed. This fortress artfully blends two distinct
Korean styles: the mountain fortress, or sanseong,
and the flat-land fortress ⓐknown as eupseong.
Historically, the sanseong served as the final defense
against invaders by utilizing Korea’s mountainous
landscape to its advantage. Defenders could fight
from higher ground and effectively ⓑpush back
enemies with fewer soldiers. A famous example of
this advantage was the battle at Haengjusanseong
during the Japanese invasion of Korea in the late
16th century.
Living in the sanseong ⓒwas not practical due to
scarce farmland and poor living conditions though.
So during peaceful times, people lived in and
around the eupseong, such as Naganeupseong and
Haemieupseong. Surrounded by low walls, the area
housed administrative buildings, learning centers,
and training grounds for soldiers. Common people,
mainly farmers, lived outside these walls. In times
of war, they withdrew to the nearby sanseong for
safety.
After the Japanese invasion, a new type of fortress
emerged ⓓthat combined the strengths of both
the sanseong and the eupseong. Built along the
natural
slopes
of
Paldalsan
Mountain,
Suwon
Hwaseong displayed strong walls and defenses
while also ⓔserved as a center for agriculture,
commerce, and housing.

The sanseong was built on mountains to usethe natural landscape as a defensive advantage.
The eupseong typically featured low walls andhoused administrative and educational facilities.
During times of war, common people stayed outsidethe walls of the eupseong for their safety.
Suwon Hwaseong represents a new style of fortress,integrating the advantages of both the sanseongand the eupseong.

body:
Today’s mission required a spacewalk, one of the
riskiest tasks on the ISS. We had to install the
bases for some newly developed solar batteries on
the outside of the station.
Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a
room (A)[connected / was connected] to the outside
of the station, put on our spacesuits, and floated
gently into space. The large blue dome of Earth
hovered overhead, (B)[looked / looking] like it was
ready to come crashing down upon us. Forcing
(C)[me / myself] to focus on the task, I secured the
hook of my safety cable to a ring just outside the
airlock. We moved along the handrail to the edge
of the station. The dark void in front of us seemed
endless. Despite the safety cable, panic rose in me.
I thought, “If my hand misses the handrail, I will fall
into the void.” The task seemed to take forever, but
I finally managed to install the battery bases. When
I turned my head, the bright blue Earth was still
there. In the middle of darkness, its beauty was
beyond description.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)               (B)           (C)
choices: connectedlookingme
was connectedlookingmyself
connectedlookedmyself
was connectedlookedme
connectedlookingmyself
solution: (A) 동사(went)가 있는 완전한 절(Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock)에 접속사 없이 쉼표로만 주어와 동사가 있는 완전한 절이 이어질 수 없으므로, a room을 주어로 하는 동사(구)는 쓰일 수 없으며, 흐름상 명사구 an airlock과 동격 의 쉼표(,)로 연결된 명사구 a room을 수식하는 분사구를 이루 는 분사가 와야 한다. 수식을 받는 명사구가 ‘connect ~ to … (~을 …에 연결하다)’의 구조를 이루는 타동사로 쓰인 connect 의 대상이므로, 수동 표현인 ‘~ be connected to …(~가 …에 연결되다)’의 과거분사 connected가 알맞다. (B) 동사(hovered)가 있는 완전한 절(The ~ overhead) 뒤에 접 속사 없이 쉼표로만 연결되어 있으므로, 분사구문을 이끄는 분 사 자리이며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 The large blue dome of Earth(지구의 거대한 푸른 돔)가 ‘보 이는’ 주체이고 ‘look like ~(~처럼 보이다)’의 look은 불완전자 동사이므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 looking이 알맞다. (C) 분사구문을 이루는 현재분사 Forcing에 이어지는 목적어 자리이며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 I와 Forcing의 목적어가 동일한 대상이므로, 재귀 용법의 대명사인 myself가 알맞다.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

The station orbits Earth once every 90 minutes, and
the sun rises and sets every 45 minutes. However, our
schedules are set to Greenwich Mean Time on Earth.
My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal
space, which is about the size of a phone booth.
Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails
and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with
a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There’s no
good way to spit in space because everything
floats. Then, I look over the daily schedule sent by
the flight control team on Earth. After a meeting
with the Earth team at 7:30, I start work.
Every minute of an astronaut’s day is planned by
the Earth team. My work comprises lots of scientific
experiments and maintenance of the station. My
favorite experiment is growing basil from seeds as I
film its growth every day. Having green plants in
space is a delight!

body:
Mother Earth didn’t exactly welcome us back with
open arms. Earth’s atmosphere is resistant to
objects ⓐentering from space. Any object will
create enough friction simply to burn up from the
heat. This protects the planet from the orbital
debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it
also meant we had to survive a fall through the
atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650
degrees Celsius.
ⓑAfter pushing our spaceship away from the
station, we eased our way into the upper layers of
the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity
ⓒbegin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on
my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule
heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces
flew by the window, ⓓwhich was scorched black.
We were falling faster than the speed of sound.
Once we got inside the atmosphere about eight
kilometers above the planet, a parachute caught us
with a sudden halt and dragged and swung our
capsule wildly through the sky until we hit the
ground.
It’s hard to describe how heavy everything felt in
those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt
terribly heavy, and ⓔso did my legs. Getting used
to gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a
long time. The important thing is I’m home. I can
smell the grass and feel the wind and the rain! I’ll
remember how magical these things are for the rest
of my life.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: which enter from space
ⓑ: After we pushed away our spaceship from thestation
ⓒ: to begin returning
ⓓ: and it was scorched black
ⓔ: my legs felt terribly heavy, too
solution: ⓒ begin은 지각동사 felt의 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 동사원형 으로, 지각동사는 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때 목 적격보어로 동사원형을 쓰고 능동·진행일 때는 현재분사를 쓰 며, 수동일 때는 과거분사를 사용한다. 그러나 지각동사의 목 적격보어로 to부정사는 쓰이지 않으므로, 동사원형인 begin을 to부정사 to begin으로 바꾼 것은 알맞지 않다. 그 외, begin 은 의미의 차이 없이 to부정사나 동명사를 목적어로 취하는 동사이므로, begin 뒤에 to부정사 to return을 동명사 returning 으로 바꿔 쓴 것은 알맞다.

I’m confident that
I’m convinced that
solution: 밑줄 친 ‘I have no doubt that ~’은 ‘나는 ~라는 것에 대한 의심의 여지가 없다’라는 뜻으로, Rays에는 3점 슛을 던질 수 있는 선수들이 많다는 것을 근거로 제시하여 Rays가 오늘 밤 경기에서 이기리라 믿어 의심치 않는다는 확실성을 나타내는 의미로 쓰였으므로, 의심이나 불확신을 나타내는 ❸ ‘I’m doubtful that ~(나는 ~라는 것이 의심스럽다)’과는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 참고로, ‘I have no doubt that ~’은 ‘I’m sure/positive/ confident/convinced that ~(나는 ~라고 확신한다)’ 등으로 바 꿔 쓸 수 있다.

body:
Sabermetrics was created in the late 1970s. It tries
to use large amounts of information to discover
patterns, trends, and insights that are difficult to
find with traditional ways of studying statistics.
Normally, coaches and managers prefer players who
can hit the ball hard and far, for such players tend
to hit more home runs and extra-base hits.
Sabermetrics suggests (A)[what / that] players’
offensive skills can be better measured by the
frequency with which they safely reach base. It does
not matter whether this is achieved through hits,
walks, or hit-by-pitches.
Sabermetrics (B)[has / had] not been widely used
until the Athletics adopted it in 2002. With
sabermetrics, the Athletics were able to identify
underrated players with significant contributions to
winning and built a strong team on a small budget.
The success of the Athletics prompted other teams
(C)[quickly adopt / to quickly adopt] sabermetrics,
sparking a movement to utilize data not only in
baseball but also in other sports. Thus, sports data
analytics emerged as a systematic approach to
predict game outcomes.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)          (B)                (C)
choices: whathas    quickly adopt
thathad    to quickly adopt
thathad    quickly adopt
thathas    to quickly adopt
whathad    to quickly adopt
solution: (A) 동사 suggests의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(players’ ~ base)을 이끌고 있으므로, 명사절 접속사인 that이 알맞다. 참 고로, 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 또는 의문대명사 what은 불완전한 절을 이끌어 문장에서 주어, 목적어, 보어 역할을 하 는 명사절을 이룬다. (B) 2002년에 애슬레틱스가 세이버메트릭스를 도입한 것이 과 거시제(adopted)로 진술되어 있으며, 그때까지 널리 사용되지 않았던 것이므로, 과거의 특정 시점(2002년) 이전부터 그때까 지의 상태를 나타내는 과거완료(had p.p.)를 이루는 완료조동 사 had가 알맞다. (C) 과거형 동사 prompted와 목적어 other teams에 이어져 ‘prompt+목적어+목적격보어’(~이 …하도록 촉구하다)의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, prompt는 목적격보어로 to 부정사를 취하는 동사이므로 to부정사구 to quickly adopt가 알맞다.

In baseball, the ball and the bat have hidden
numbers that can greatly impact the outcome of a
game. A baseball has 108 double stitches, creating
raised lines on the ball called seams. (A)솔기는 투수
가 공을 더 잘 잡고, 그것을 던질 때 더 많은 힘과 회
전을 전달할 수 있도록 도와준다. A spinning ball can
change directions in the air because of the air
pressure around it. This is called the Magnus effect.
The seams make this effect stronger. Pitchers can
use this effect to control the ball’s direction and
speed, creating pitches that are difficult for batters
to hit.
While pitchers try to throw challenging pitches by
utilizing the ball’s seams, batters attempt to make
contact with the ball accurately in the hope of
hitting a home run. The secret to hitting a home
run lies in the baseball bat. The bat’s overall length
must be less than 106.8 cm long and the diameter
of the thickest part must be less than 7 cm. If a
player hits the ball about 5-10 cm from the end of
the bat, the ball will fly the farthest and give the
player the most thrilling and sweetest feeling. That
is why this area is called the “sweet spot.”

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: evolution of baseball rules and regulations
importance of physical training for pitchers andbatters
psychological factors impacting performance ofbaseball players
ways to choose the right baseball bat for higherbatting average
how the ball’s seams and the bat’s sweet spotshape baseball results
solution: 야구공의 108개 이중 바늘땀이 만들어내는 솔기가 투수로 하 여금 공을 더 잘 잡도록, 그리고 더 많은 힘과 회전을 전달할 수 있도록 도와주며, 배트 끝에서 약 5~10cm 떨어진 지점을 일컫는 ‘스위트 스팟’으로 공을 치면 공이 가장 멀리 날아간다 고 했으므로, 글의 주제로 ❺ ‘공의 솔기와 배트의 스위트 스 팟이 어떻게 야구 경기 결과를 결정짓는지’가 알맞다.

market?

Neil: How does that work?
Beth: Let’s imagine that a small group of people
start a footwear company producing innovative
sneakers. The founders are confident that
their products will be popular with consumers,
but they do not have enough funds to grow
the business. So they decide to put the newly
formed company on the stock market.
Neil: What happens then?

individuals or organizations that believe in the
company’s bright future can buy shares and
become partial owners of the company. This
process makes it easy for the footwear
company to raise the funds it needs to grow
its business. As the business grows, the stock
value rises, and the stockholders’ profits increase.

demand. In other words, the more successful
a business is, the more people will see the
potential value of the company and start
ⓐbuying its stocks. As demand for the stocks
increases, so does the stock price. In contrast,
if a company ⓑwill perform disappointingly,
its stock price will fall.

there

Stock market movement can be divided into two
major trends: bull market vs. bear market.
BULL MARKET
A bull market is a ⓐrising stock market situation
in which economic conditions are favorable to
investors. They include high employment rates, GDP
increases, and other positive economic indicators.
ⓑThinking of a charging bull in a field raising its
horns. In a bull market, investors often (A)__________
__________________________________________. As such, they
increase their stock purchases and ⓒmaintaining
their investments.
BEAR MARKET
Like a standing bear ⓓhaving lowered its front
legs, a bear market implies a decline in stock values.
It ⓔis occurred when economic conditions are not
favorable, and most stocks experience decreases in
value. Factors like low GDP growth, rising unemployment,
and low wages ⓕare possible conditions for a bear
market. In difficult economic situations, investors
frequently have negative views of the stock market,
which may lead them to sell their stocks.

podcast for teenagers! I’m your host, Neil.
Thank you for tuning in. We have a very
special guest with us, the renowned economist
Beth Friedman. Please give her a warm
welcome!
Beth: Hello, everyone. It’s truly an honor to be here
with all of you.
Neil: We’ve been exploring the basics of economics.
In this 35th episode, we’ll be talking about the
world of stocks. So let’s get started.
Beth: Before we begin, Neil, I have a question for
you. Have you ever wondered what to do
with your extra money?
Neil: Absolutely, Beth. I bet all our listeners have
asked themselves the same question.
Beth: Indeed. It’s a question that often arises,
especially among young people who are
beginning to explore the world of finance. As
you go about your daily lives, you find
yourself engaged in financial activities such as
purchasing goods and paying bus fares. After
that, you might have some extra money.

다음 대화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

B: Did you know ⓐthat astronauts perform several
experiments on the International Space Station?
G: Yes. A good example of them ⓑare growing
lettuce in space.
B: Astronauts had to prove it was safe ⓒto eat in
a harsh environment with lots of radiation.
G: Right. Safety is important. I think they must ⓓ
have been excited to eat fresh lettuce in space.
B: Absolutely! They said it was not only fresh and
tasty but also free of radiation.
G: I’m amazed at ⓔhow far space farming has
advanced. It’s revolutionary. Don’t you think so?
B: I do. It’s incredible! It seems like the day ⓕ
which astronauts can enjoy dinner with fresh
ingredients in space is not far away.
solution: ⓑ are → is (주어부 ‘A good example of them’에 이어진 문장의 동사 자 리로, 뒤에 온 동명사구(growing ~ space)를 보어로 취할 수 있는 be동사가 흐름상 현재시제로 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 주어 부의 핵심 단어인 example이 단수명사이므로, 이에 수일치된 단수동사 is로 고친다.) ⓕ which → when[that, on which] 또는 which 삭제 (완전한 절(astronauts can ~ in space)을 이끌어 선행사 the day를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 불완전한 절을 이끄는 which를 시간의 관계부사 when으로 고친다. 선행사가 day인 경우 when 대신 관계부사 대용의 that을 쓰거나 생략할 수 있고, 관계부사는 선행사에 어울리는 전치사를 사용해 ‘전치 사+관계대명사’로 바꿔 쓸 수 있으므로, which를 that으로 고 치거나 which를 삭제하는 것도 가능하며, day와 어울리는 전치 사 on을 사용해 ‘전치사+관계대명사’인 on which로 고칠 수도 있다.)

body:
Day 1 Back to Space!
After ⓐblasting off from Earth, we took about 27
hours to reach the International Space Station,
where we docked successfully. This is my third
journey into space. After ten years, I’m back on this
station, the largest artificial space habitat in orbit
400 kilometers away from Earth!
Day 5 The World with No Gravity
Now I’m getting better at ⓑforgetting where I am
when I first wake up, but I’m still often confused
about how my body is positioned. In the dark and
without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random
guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up
ⓒconvinced that I’m upside down. Of course, it’s
actually my brain readjusting to an environment
where height and weight lose their meaning. I can
use any wall ⓓequally as if each were a floor.
Everything has zero weight. (A)이것은 내가 날아다닐
수 있을 뿐 아니라 수퍼히어로가 된 것처럼 큰 사물들을
손가락 하나로 들어올릴 수 있게 한다. Unfortunately,
zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and
bone density really ⓔslowly. That’s why I exercise
for 150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

I’ll return to Earth tomorrow.
(A) All the same, I’ll never forget how lucky we are
to have that wonderful blue planet as our home.
(B) If getting up into space is alarming and
uncomfortable, coming back down is one of
the most dangerous and physically harsh things
an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I’ll miss
lots of things here.
(C) I’ll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing
an experiment or a challenging task like a
spacewalk. I’ll especially miss my basil plants,
whose leaves have become a dense forest!
solution: 내일 지구로 돌아간다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 우주로 올 라가는 일이 두렵고 불편하다면, 지구로 귀환하는 것은 우주 비행사가 하는 일 중 가장 위험하고 육체적으로 가혹한 일 중 하나라는 내용과, 지구로 돌아가면 이곳의 많은 것들이 그리울 것이라는 (B), 앞서 언급된 이곳(우주)에서의 많은 것들과 관련 된 구체적 예시로서, 실험이나 우주 유영같이 도전적인 업무를 성공적으로 마쳤을 때의 만족감과, 특히 하나의 울창한 숲을 이룬 바질 식물들이 그리울 것이라는 (C), ‘그래도’라는 뜻의 역접의 접속부사 All the same에 연결되어 (C)에 언급된 그리 운 것들에도 불구하고 저 아름다운 푸른 행성을 우리의 집으 로 가진 것이 얼마나 행운인지 늘 잊지 않을 것이라는 대조적 인 내용으로 마무리하는 (A)의 흐름이 자연스럽다. YBM(박준언) 5과

body:
Day 60 Spacewalk!
Today’s mission required a spacewalk, one of the
(A)[riskiest / easiest] tasks on the ISS. We had to
install the bases for some newly developed solar
batteries on the outside of the station.
Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a
room connected to the outside of the station, put
on our spacesuits, and floated gently into space.
The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead,
looking like it was ready to come crashing down
upon us. Forcing myself to (B)[give up / focus on]
the task, I secured the hook of my safety cable to
a ring just outside the airlock. We moved along
the handrail to the edge of the station. The dark
void in front of us seemed endless. Despite the
safety cable, (C)[panic / calmness] rose in me. I
thought, “If my hand misses the handrail, I will fall
into the void.” ⓐ그 작업은 끝없이 걸릴 것처럼 보였
지만, 마침내 나는 배터리 받침대들을 설치해 내었다.
When I turned my head, the bright blue Earth was
still there. In the middle of darkness, its beauty was
beyond description.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: easiestfocus onpanic
easiestgive upcalmness
riskiestgive uppanic
riskiestfocus onpanic
riskiestfocus oncalmness
solution: (A) 안전줄에 의지하며 우주에 몸을 띄운 채 태양열 전지를 위 한 받침대를 우주정거장 외부에 설치하는 업무를 해야 했으므 로, 우주 유영이 ISS에서 하는 가장 위험한 업무 중 하나라는 흐름이 되는 riskiest(가장 위험한)가 알맞다. (B) 글쓴이가 안전줄의 고리를 에어록 바로 바깥쪽 원형 고리 에 걸었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 그녀가 지구의 거대한 푸른 돔이 자신의 머리 위에 부딪힐 듯이 떠 있었음에도, 작업에 집 중하도록 스스로를 다잡았다는 흐름이 되는 focus on(~에 집 중하다)이 알맞다. (C) 글쓴이가 자신의 바로 앞 컴컴한 허공이 끝이 없어 보였다 고 했으며, 자신이 난간을 놓치면 저 허공 속으로 떨어질 것이 라고 생각했으므로, 안전줄에도 불구하고 그녀 안에서 공포가 올라왔다는 흐름이 되는 panic(공포)이 알맞다.

body:
Mother Earth didn’t exactly welcome us back with
open arms. Earth’s atmosphere is resistant to
objects entering from space. Any object will create
enough friction simply to burn up from the heat.
This protects the planet from the orbital debris that
would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant
(A)[that / what] we had to survive a fall through
the atmosphere that created temperatures up to
1650 degrees Celsius.
After pushing our spaceship away from the station,
we eased our way into the upper layers of the
atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity
begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my
wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated
up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by
the window, (B)[which / where] was scorched black.
We were falling faster than the speed of sound.
Once we got inside the atmosphere about eight
kilometers above the planet, a parachute caught us
with a sudden halt and dragged and swung our
capsule wildly through the sky until we hit the ground.
It’s hard to describe how heavy everything felt in
those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt
terribly heavy, and so (C)[did / were] my legs.
Getting used to gravity, which I missed in space,
will take quite a long time. The important thing is
ⓐ_______________________________. I can smell the grass
and feel the wind and the rain! I’ll remember how
magical these things are for the rest of my life.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)         (B)        (C)
choices: thatwheredid
whatwhichdid
thatwhichwere
whatwherewere
thatwhichdid
solution: (A) meant의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(we ~　Celsius)을 이 끌고 있으므로, 명사절 접속사인 that이 알맞다. 참고로, 관계 대명사 또는 의문대명사 what은 뒤에 주어나 목적어, 보어가 없는 불완전한 절이 이어져 명사절을 이룬다. (B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was scorched black)을 이끌어 쉼표 앞의 명사구 the window를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어 야 하므로, 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. (C) 긍정 내용의 완전한 절(My ~ heavy) 뒤에 쉼표(,)와 등위접 속사 and로 연결되어 ‘~도 또한 그렇다’라는 뜻의 ‘so+동사+ 주어’ 형태의 도치 구문을 이루는 동사 자리이므로, 앞 절에 쓰인 일반동사 felt의 반복을 피하기 위한 과거시제의 대동사 did가 알맞다.

body:
The International Space Station, or ISS, is the ninth
space station to be inhabited by humans. Since
2000,
it
has
been
continuously
occupied
by
astronauts. It serves as a research laboratory for
many fields, including astronomy, physics, and
medicine. It is also used to test spacecraft systems
required for possible future missions to the moon,
Mars, and asteroids. As big as a football field, it is
composed of many different sections, such as
experiment
modules,
habitation
modules,
solar
battery panels, and robotic arms. It is a completely
unique structure assembled by spacewalkers flying
around Earth at 28,000 kilometers per hour in a
vacuum in extremes of temperature of plus and
minus 270 degrees Celsius. It is the result of work
by 15 different nations over about two decades.
The work was carried out by thousands of people
speaking different languages and using different
engineering methods and standards. Putting the
space station into orbit, making it work, and
keeping it working are perhaps some of the most
difficult things that human beings have ever done.
In January 2022, NASA announced a plan to
de-orbit the ISS in 2030. Many astronauts believe
that it will stand forever as proof that ______________
_____________________________________________ from going
to Mars to solving our problems here on Earth.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: we can predict technological progress
we should find new alternatives to the ISS
when humans work together, we can do anything
human ambition can lead to unexpected disasters
though space is vast, we must conquer it bydoing something
solution: 국제우주정거장은 섭씨 영상, 영하 270도의 극한을 오가는 진 공 속에서 시속 2만 8천 킬로미터로 지구 주위를 날아다니는 우주 유영자들이 조립한 완벽하게 독특한 구조물로, 약 20년 동안 15개의 국가가 협력하여 이끌어 낸 결과물이라고 했으므 로, 인간의 협력을 통한다면 화성 탐사에서부터 이곳 지구 문 제의 해결에 이르기까지 못할 것이 없음을 국제우주정거장이 증명할 것이라는 흐름이 되는 ❸ ‘인간이 협력하면, 우리는 무 엇이건 해낼 수 있다’가 알맞다.

course, it’s actually my brain readjusting to an
environment where height and weight lose their
meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each were
a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me
not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with
one finger as if I were a superhero. Unfortunately,
zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and
bone density really fast. That’s why I exercise for
150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.

The International Space Station, or ISS, is the ninth
space station to be inhabited by humans. Since
2000,
it
has
been
continuously
occupied
by
astronauts. It serves as a research laboratory for
many fields, including astronomy, physics, and
medicine. It is also used to test spacecraft systems
required for possible future missions to the moon,
Mars, and asteroids. As big as a football field, it is
composed of many different sections, such as
experiment
modules,
habitation
modules,
solar
battery panels, and robotic arms. It is a completely
unique structure assembled by spacewalkers flying
around Earth at 28,000 kilometers per hour in a
vacuum in extremes of temperature of plus and
minus 270 degrees Celsius. It is the result of work
by 15 different nations over about two decades.
The work was carried out by thousands of people
speaking different languages and using different
engineering methods and standards. Putting the
space station into orbit, making it work, and
keeping it working are perhaps some of the most
difficult things that human beings have ever done.
In January 2022, NASA announced a plan to
de-orbit the ISS in 2030. Many astronauts believe
that it will stand forever as proof that ______________
_____________________________________________ from going

Mother Earth didn’t exactly welcome us back with
open arms. Earth’s atmosphere is resistant to
objects entering from space. Any object will create
enough friction simply to burn up from the heat.
This protects the planet from the orbital debris that
would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant
we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere
that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees
Celsius.
After pushing our spaceship away from the station,
we eased our way into the upper layers of the
atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity
begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my
wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated
up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by
the window, which was scorched black. We were
falling faster than the speed of sound. Once we got
inside the atmosphere about eight kilometers above
the planet, a parachute caught us with a sudden
halt and dragged and swung our capsule wildly
through the sky until we hit the ground.
It’s hard to describe how heavy everything felt in
those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt
terribly heavy, and so did my legs. Getting used to
gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a
long time. The important thing is I’m home. I can
smell the grass and feel the wind and the rain! I’ll
remember how magical these things are for the rest
of my life.
